name: Magnitude
tagline: Open source inference engine for agents that tunes its kernels to your hardware
summary: Magnitude is a desktop app and CLI that runs open-weight models locally. It compiles and tunes its kernels on the user's own device before a model runs, shares prefix caches across concurrent agent sessions, and works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD or a CPU alone. One click connects coding agents such as Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code and Cline, and anything else can use its OpenAI-compatible API.
watching: It is a local model server built for coding agents, the same role Ollama and llama.cpp play behind the desktop's Local Llama provider, and its OpenAI-compatible API is the kind of endpoint that provider accepts.

comparison.project: An inference engine, desktop app and CLI that run open-weight models locally for coding agents.
comparison.forkmesh: An open-source network for hosting, mirroring and collaborating on Git repositories, with coding agents as one part of its desktop app.

name: rhun
tagline: Small, fast code editor written in assembly, with a terminal, Git and an agents panel
summary: rhun is a code editor for Linux, Windows and Apple Silicon Macs whose editor and pixel renderer are handwritten x86-64 assembly, translated to AArch64 at build time. It has tabs, syntax highlighting, fuzzy file and project search, an optional Vim mode and a built-in terminal. Its Git view stages, commits, pulls and pushes, shows diffs and history, and can draft commit messages with a Claude or Codex subscription or a local Ollama model. An agents panel shows Claude Code and Codex sessions as they work.
watching: It is built for the workflow where coding agents write the code and a person reads diffs, runs commands and commits, the same split the desktop's agent worktrees assume, and it watches Claude Code and Codex sessions beside the editor.

comparison.project: A small code editor written in x86-64 assembly, with a terminal, a Git view and an agents panel.

name: Zide
tagline: Native desktop workspace for code, Git, issues, pull requests, CI, terminals and AI agents
summary: Zide is a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, built with Tauri and Rust, that puts an editor with language servers, a full Git client (hunk staging, interactive rebase, bisect, worktrees, submodules, LFS), terminals, a browser and a multi-repository workspace in one window. It connects to GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab and Bitbucket for issues, pull or merge requests, reviews and CI. Its agent, Zide Assist, works across files and repositories on hosted, bring-your-own-key or local models; QuickTree starts a worktree from a prompt, Crosscheck sends each agent commit to a second reviewer model, and CLI agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Gemini run alongside it.
watching: It is the closest desktop counterpart to ForkMesh's own: issues, worktrees, coding agents, diffs, pull requests and CI in one native app. It takes the opposite position on hosting, leaving repositories and collaboration on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.

comparison.project: A desktop workspace that brings an editor, a Git client, issues, pull requests, CI and AI agents to repositories hosted elsewhere.
comparison.forkmesh: A network for hosting, mirroring and collaborating on repositories, with a desktop app as one of its clients.

comparison.forkmesh: On developer-operated nodes and signed mirrors; a stable URL clones from whichever mirror is healthy.

comparison.project: Read and acted on through the host's API: issues from GitHub and GitLab, pull or merge requests and CI from all three hosts.
comparison.forkmesh: Signed records stored in the repository under .forkmesh/, so they travel with the code; a pull request to an offline owner is queued.

name: Fossil
tagline: Distributed version control with a built-in bug tracker, wiki, forum, chat and web interface
summary: Fossil is a distributed version control system from the makers of SQLite. One self-contained executable carries version control together with bug tracking, a wiki, a forum, email alerts, chat, technotes and a themeable web interface, so a project website can be stood up in minutes on a small VPS or a Raspberry Pi. A repository is a single SQLite database with atomic transactions, and autosync sends each commit to the parent repository straight away. It syncs over HTTPS or SSH, has no rebase by design, and can mirror a repository to GitHub, though tickets and wiki do not carry over to a Git mirror.
watching: Fossil has long kept a project's tickets, wiki and forum alongside its code in one repository that every clone carries. ForkMesh makes the same choice for Git, storing issues, pull requests and reviews as signed records under .forkmesh/ in the repository.
maker: D. Richard Hipp and the Fossil developers

comparison.project: A distributed version control system with bug tracking, wiki, forum, chat and a web interface built into one executable.
comparison.forkmesh: An open-source network for hosting, mirroring and collaborating on Git repositories.

comparison.project: Its own format: each repository is a single SQLite database, and history cannot be rebased or squashed.
comparison.forkmesh: Works with stock Git; clones, pushes and branches are ordinary Git operations.

comparison.project: Tickets, wiki pages, forum posts and technotes live in the same repository database as the code and sync with it.
comparison.forkmesh: Issues, pull requests and reviews are signed records stored in the repository under .forkmesh/, so they travel with the code.

comparison.forkmesh: Repositories live on developer-operated nodes and core nodes, any node can mirror a public repository, and relays can be self-hosted.
